item.title: Nitrofuran metabolite found in prepackaged frozen shrimp sample
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department today (October 5) announced that a trace amount of metabolite (AOZ) of furazolidone (a type of nitrofurans), a non-permitted veterinary drug, was found in a sample of prepackaged frozen shrimp. Members of the public should not consume the affected batch of the product. The trade should also stop using or selling the affected batch of the product immediately if they possess it. The CFS is following up on the incident.

     Product details are as follows: 

Product name: (Not available in English) 
Place of origin: China 
Distributor: Linson Global Seafood Trading Limited 
Weight: 200 grams 
Best-before date: January 22, 2028

     A spokesman for the CFS said, "The CFS collected the shrimp sample from a fresh provision shop in North Point for testing under its routine Food Surveillance Programme. The test result showed that it contained AOZ at a level of 6.1 parts per billion." 

     "The CFS has informed the vendor concerned of the irregularity and instructed it to stop sale and remove from shelves the affected batch of the product. According to the CFS's instructions, the distributor has initiated a recall of the affected batch of the product. Members of the public may call its hotline at 2573 7433 during office hours for enquiries about the recall of the product concerned," the spokesman added.

     The CFS will alert the trade, and will continue to follow up on the incident and take appropriate action. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Matching session and kick-off ceremony of 14th Microfilm Production Support Scheme (Music) held (with photo)
item.description:
Sponsored by the Cultural and Creative Industries Development Agency (CCIDA) under the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau and organised by the Hong Kong Association of Interactive Marketing, the 14th Microfilm Production Support Scheme (Music) held its matching session and kick-off ceremony today (October 5), promoting cross-sector collaboration among Hong Kong's advertising, film and television, and music industries.
 
     Speaking at the kick-off ceremony, Assistant Commissioner for Cultural and Creative Industries Miss Yvonne Ip noted that since its launch, the scheme has facilitated collaboration between more than 340 advertising production companies and some 290 groups of singers, providing the local film and television, advertising, and music sectors with a valuable creation platform and hands-on opportunities. CCIDA will continue to actively foster cross-sector collaboration in the local creative industries, with a view to promoting the professionalism, industrialisation and internationalisation of the industries.
 
     This year's scheme consists of two funding categories, namely the "Advertising Production Start-ups" and the "Professional Advertising Production Houses". The selected creative teams will receive production funding as well as professional training and mentoring opportunities to produce original microfilms. At the kick-off ceremony, 10 start-up advertising production companies under the category of "Advertising Production Start-ups" were paired with singers, while the five teams under the category of "Professional Advertising Production Houses" were formed by directors, scriptwriters, singers and advertising production companies individually. The microfilms will premiere online in January next year and will be showcased to the industry at the Hong Kong International Film and TV Market (FILMART) in March next year.
 
     Launched in 2013, the Microfilm Production Support Scheme (Music) is a cross-sector collaboration initiative that brings together advertising and film production with music creation. It aims to enable local emerging directors and their creative teams to collaborate with local singers in producing original microfilms, thereby promoting the development of Hong Kong’s creative industry ecosystem.
 
     For more information about the 14th Microfilm Production Support Scheme (Music), please visit www.hkmfa.hk (Chinese only).

item.title: Hong Kong Customs and Hong Kong Police's Sham Shui Po District conduct joint-operation to combat illicit cigarettes (with photo)
item.description:
Hong Kong Customs and Sham Shui Po District of the Hong Kong Police Force mounted a joint-enforcement operation from September 18 to 30 and detected cases involving illicit cigarettes in the district. A total of about 100 000 illicit cigarettes with an estimated market value of about $480,000, and a duty potential of about $350,000 were seized. Five persons connected with the cases were arrested.

     To combat illicit cigarette activities in Sham Shui Po District, Customs and the Police's Sham Shui Po District conducted multiple surprise inspections and raids, cracking down on 22 temporary illicit cigarette storage points and a mobile illicit cigarette stall. Two local men, two local women and a Vietnamese man were arrested. 
      
     Customs will continue the multipronged enforcement strategy to vigorously combat illicit cigarette activities. Customs reminds members of the public that under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109), anyone involved in dealing with, possession of, selling or buying illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years.

     Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080, its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Two incoming passengers convicted and jailed for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes (with photos)
item.description:
Two incoming passengers were respectively sentenced to four and eight months’ imprisonment and each fined $2,000 by the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts today (October 5) for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes and failing to declare them to Customs officers, in contravention of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO).

     Customs officers intercepted an incoming 54-year-old Mainland female passenger arriving in Hong Kong from Tokyo, Japan, at Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA) on April 14 and seized about 12 000 duty-not-paid cigarettes, with an estimated market value of about $50,000 and a duty potential of about $40,000, from her personal baggage. The passenger was subsequently arrested.

     In addition, Customs officers intercepted an incoming 31-year-old Mainland male passenger arriving in Hong Kong from Tokyo, Japan, at HKIA on October 3 and seized a total of about 38 200 duty-not-paid cigarettes, with an estimated market value of about $172,000 and a duty potential of about $126,000, from his personal baggage. The passenger was subsequently arrested.

     Customs welcomes the sentences. The custodial sentences have imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflect the seriousness of the offences. 

     Customs reminds members of the public that under the DCO, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. 

     Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account (crimereport@customs.gov.hk) or online form (eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002).

item.title: Fourth-term Human Resources Planning Commission convenes seventh meeting
item.description:
The Chief Secretary for Administration, Mr Chan Kwok-ki, today (October 5) chaired the seventh meeting of the fourth-term Human Resources Planning Commission.
 
     At the meeting, the Census and Statistics Department briefed members on the latest situation and characteristics of Hong Kong's labour force, employment and population. Under the influence of factors such as population ageing, Hong Kong's overall labour force participation rate has been on a downward trend, which has nevertheless been alleviated by the various talent admission and labour importation measures. Members noted that the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate increased slightly from 3.7 per cent in May-July 2026 to 3.8 per cent in June-August 2026, and that the youth unemployment situation warrants attention. Members understood that the rise in unemployment and the youth employment situation are structural challenges faced by most advanced economies worldwide, and Hong Kong is no exception. They were also pleased to note that the Government continues to invest heavily in education and skills training to enhance the skills and competitiveness of the local workforce, including launching the two-year 30 000 Youth Employment and Internship Programme announced in the 2026 Policy Address to facilitate youth employment and development. The Labour Department will also launch the "Youth Employment Link" online service portal to facilitate young people's access to employment information and support services. Looking ahead, the continued expansion of the local economy is expected to underpin overall labour market conditions.
 
     The Labour and Welfare Bureau (LWB) also briefed members at the meeting on the results of the report on the Mid-term Update of Manpower Projection. The report indicates that the overall manpower shortage in Hong Kong has been alleviated, benefiting from the various talent admission and labour importation measures implemented by the Government over the past three years. The overall manpower shortage in 2028 is projected to narrow from the previous projection of approximately 180 000 to some 130 000. The demand for emerging AI experts continues to grow, particularly for "composite talent" who possesses both AI application skills and sector-specific knowledge. The Government will formulate corresponding measures in response to the results of the mid-term update, including strengthening local training and enhancing the talent admission measures. Members were pleased to note that the Government will continue to promote "AI for All" and support lifelong learning, ensuring that the skills of the labour force remain aligned with Hong Kong's future economy.

     The Hong Kong's First Five-Year plan promulgated in the middle of last month clearly sets out that, on the premise of protecting local workers, the Government will closely monitor changes in labour supply and demand, and dynamically adjust the types and number of workers to be imported.
 
     The LWB will soon commence a new round of review of the Talent List. In the course of the review, reference will be made to the latest developments of various industries and the manpower demand situation as set out in the report, with the addition of more talent categories relating to AI application. Members expressed their views on the review at the meeting and supported the Government in continuing to closely monitor the labour market and in formulating and refining forward-looking manpower policies on a rolling basis, with a view to maintaining manpower supply to support economic development while safeguarding the employment priority for local workers.
 
     Members also received a briefing from the Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau on the latest progress in promoting new industrialisation in Hong Kong, covering the overall strategy and key measures. The briefing set out how Hong Kong will drive industrial transformation and reshape a new industrialisation system with distinctive local advantages through a series of measures to accelerate the translation of mid-stream research outcomes and support downstream industrial development, including sustaining traditional industries through technological upgrading and transformation; cultivating emerging industries to accelerate their integration into and serve the nation's modern industrial system; planning for future industries to seize the first-mover advantage for high-quality development; and strengthening producer services. Members recognised the Government's efforts in promoting new industrialisation, and hoped to see Hong Kong's competitive advantages consolidated and sustainable economic development fostered.

item.title: CHP records case of severe paediatric influenza infection
item.description:
​​The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 5) recorded a severe paediatric influenza infection case. The CHP urged the public to receive vaccinations as early as possible to safeguard their own health and that of their families. In addition, the public should maintain good personal and environmental hygiene at all times to prevent influenza and other respiratory illnesses.

     The case involves a 10-year-old boy with good past health. He developed a fever, cough, runny nose and dizziness on October 2. He was brought to the Accident and Emergency Department of Prince of Wales Hospital on October 4. He was admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit for treatment on the same day. His respiratory specimen tested positive for influenza A (H1) virus. His clinical diagnosis was influenza A infection complicated with shock. The patient remains hospitalised and is in serious condition.

     The CHP's preliminary investigation revealed that the patient had no travel history during the incubation period, and had not received the 2026/27 Seasonal Influenza Vaccination (SIV). One of his household contacts recently developed a mild fever and upper respiratory symptoms, but the symptoms were mild and the household contact concerned has recovered. The CHP will continue to investigate the case.

     Hong Kong entered the influenza season in late June. The latest surveillance data showed that influenza activity remains at a high level. Since the end of June, a cumulative total of 22 cases of severe paediatric influenza infection have been recorded. Among these cases, 16 patients have recovered and been discharged from hospital, two patients are in stable condition, two are in serious condition, one is in critical condition and one has passed away. Due to widespread influenza transmission in the community in recent months, there has been a significant increase in both the number of infections and severe cases. Since the new school year started in September, nearly 350 influenza-like illness outbreaks have been recorded in schools, affecting over 2 000 persons. Therefore, schools and parents must remain vigilant and take preventive measures.

     The 2026/27 SIV Programmes, including the SIV School Outreach Programme (SIVSOP), commenced on September 17. The SIVSOP this year has introduced a new Electronic Consent Form (e-consent form) feature via eHealth. This new measure not only facilitates the public to join the SIV Programmes but also streamlines the administrative procedures for healthcare service providers and schools, so that SIV outreach activities can start as early as possible. Approximately 100 schools have organised SIV outreach activities, a significant increase compared to the same period last year. SIV outreach activities are expected to be completed by mid-December, about two weeks earlier than last year. The CHP appeals to all schools and parents in Hong Kong to work closely with the CHP and complete the consent process as soon as possible so that students can be arranged to receive SIV earlier.

     The CHP reminds parents that the health condition of children with influenza can deteriorate rapidly. Parents must pay close attention to their condition, and visit an accident and emergency department immediately if the child's condition deteriorates with symptoms such as shortness of breath, wheezing, blue lips, chest pain, confusion, a persistent fever or convulsions. Members of the public should seek medical attention as soon as possible if they develop respiratory symptoms. If they live with members of high-risk groups, such as children, the elderly and those with underlying illnesses or compromised immune systems, they should wear a surgical mask at home to reduce the risk of infecting them. Other effective ways to reduce the spread of the disease include maintaining household hygiene, frequently cleaning and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces, practising good hand hygiene, and ensuring proper indoor air circulation.

     Members of the public may refer to the CHP's COVID-19 & Flu Express, Seasonal Influenza Webpage and Vaccination Schemes for the latest information.

item.title: ICH Office launches new exhibition "Living Craftsmanship" (with photos)
item.description:
The ​"Living Craftsmanship - Hong Kong Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition", presented by the Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) Office under the Leisure and Cultural Services Department, will be open to the public from tomorrow (October 6) at CLP Pulse, which has been revitalised from a Grade 1 historic building. The exhibition invites visitors to explore the dedication and skills of ICH practitioners, the historical and cultural significance behind these crafts, and stories of their transmission.

     The exhibition features eight ICH items related to Hong Kong’s traditional craftsmanship, including Technique of Making Kwan Kwa Wedding Costume, Flower Button Making Technique, Paper Crafting Technique, Cantonese Opera Headdress Crafting Technique, Wooden Boat Building Technique, Steamer Making Technique, Mahjong Tile Making Technique, and Guangcai (Canton Famille Rose Porcelain) Making Technique. In addition to showcasing exquisite ICH works that convey the warmth of craftsmanship and relevant production tools, the exhibition is supplemented by interactive multimedia programmes, vividly presenting the vitality of traditional crafts in contemporary society.

     CLP Pulse is located at 147 Argyle Street, Ho Man Tin, Kowloon. Admission is free. For details of the exhibition, please visit the ICH Office website at www.icho.hk/en/web/icho/living_craftsmanship.html.

     The exhibition is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series. Please visit www.lcsd.gov.hk/en/ccpo/index.html for more information.

item.title: DH responds to media enquiries regarding "Heal Fertility Limited"
item.description:
In response to media enquiries regarding "Heal Fertility Limited" (the centre), which was previously requested to stop accepting new cases for reproductive technology procedures following a Serious Untoward Event involving a mix-up in embryo biopsy specimens, the Department of Health (DH) announced today (October 5) that in light of the confirmation by the Council on Human Reproductive Technology (Council) that the centre has properly implemented all remedial and improvement measures, and has been approved by the Council to fully resume all 17 treatment services covered by its licence from tomorrow (October 6), the DH lifted its earlier directive suspending the centre from accepting new patients for assisted reproductive technology procedures. Starting tomorrow, the centre will be able to fully resume accepting new patients for assisted reproductive technology procedures.

     Regarding the centre's failure to report the Serious Untoward Events to the DH within 24 hours of identification, as required by the Code of Practice for Day Procedure Centres (Code of Practice) under the Private Healthcare Facilities Ordinance (Cap. 633) (the Ordinance), the DH completed an investigation and issued a press release early last month stating that the centre had implemented a series of improvement measures as directed by the DH to prevent the recurrence of similar incidents and to ensure strict compliance in the future with the Code of Practice, which requires reporting any Serious Untoward Events to the DH within 24 hours of identification. If there is non-compliance to the Code of Practice by licensed private healthcare facilities, the DH will take regulatory action according to the risk level posed by the non-compliance to patient safety. 

     The DH once again reminded all private healthcare facilities holding licences from the Council to provide reproductive technology procedures that they must strictly comply with the relevant licensing conditions and the Codes of Practice stipulated by the DH and the Council. The DH will continue to monitor the compliance of licensed private healthcare facilities with the requirements of the Ordinance, the licensing conditions, and the Code of Practice, in order to safeguard public safety.

item.title: Council on Human Reproductive Technology approves full resumption of services at "Heal Fertility Limited"
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Council on Human Reproductive Technology:
      
     The Council on Human Reproductive Technology (Council) convened a special meeting today (October 5) to review the licence of "Heal Fertility Limited" (Heal Fertility). In view of the earlier incident involving a mix-up in embryo biopsy specimens at Heal Fertility, Council members thoroughly reviewed the information obtained from a follow-up on-site inspection, and confirmed that Heal Fertility has properly implemented all remedial and improvement measures. Therefore, the Council allowed Heal Fertility to fully resume all 17 treatment services covered by its licence starting tomorrow (October 6).
      
     Since July 8, the Council had suspended Heal Fertility's 14 treatment services out of 17, with the exception of three services related to the storage of gametes or embryos, and had set up an investigation committee to investigate the matter. The Council had convened a special meeting on September 3 to review the investigation report and the licence matters of Heal Fertility.  
      
     This meeting followed up on a special meeting held by the Council on September 3 regarding the same incident. At that time, the Council accepted its conclusion that the main cause of the incident may involve intentional unlawful conduct by an individual, and considered that there is still room for further enhancement in Heal Fertility's overall performance and operational arrangements following the incident. Consequently, on September 4, the Council sent a letter to Heal Fertility, explicitly requiring Heal Fertility to duly carry out a set of concrete improvement measures to prevent a recurrence of similar incidents. Until Heal Fertility had properly implemented the measures, it could only continue to provide three services related to the storage of gametes or embryos. 
      
     On September 22, the Council conducted another unannounced on‑site inspection of Heal Fertility, focusing on all aspects of the remedial measures.
      
     The Council was satisfied and convinced that Heal Fertility had refined its internal sample‑handling procedures, strengthened staff training, and upgraded laboratory management and security systems in accordance with the Council's requirements, including the implementation of CCTV surveillance on the premises, the installation of biometric locks on all cryostorage tanks, and the enhancement of sample identification and verification. The Council also noted that the main personnel involved in the incident had already left Heal Fertility, and that Heal Fertility has recruited new staff and provided training. After thoroughly reviewing the relevant reports and inspection results, the Council therefore allowed Heal Fertility to resume normal operations starting tomorrow. The Council will continue to closely monitor Heal Fertility's performance to safeguard the continuous provision of safe and high-quality services to individuals seeking human reproductive technology services.
      
     Moreover, the Council has commenced a review of the Code of Practice on Reproductive Technology and Embryo Research. Key areas include reviewing the incident reporting mechanism and optimising the security and handling procedures of biological samples, with a target completion date of next year.

item.title: Guard against fake messages claiming direct whole-day use of new Huanggang Port for vehicles under Guangdong-Hong Kong Regular Quotas
item.description:
A Government spokesman today (October 5) urged the public not to be misled by fake messages on social media that claim vehicles of Guangdong-Hong Kong Regular Quota holders issued with Closed Road Permits (CRPs) for the Heung Yuen Wai/Liantang Port, Shenzhen Bay Port or Sha Tau Kok Control Point (collectively referred to as designated control points) can directly use the new Huanggang Port to cross the boundary throughout the day. The case will be referred to law enforcement agencies for follow-up.

     Applicants for the Guangdong-Hong Kong Regular Quotas must currently satisfy the application qualifications set by the Mainland authorities and submit designated application documents (such as business registration documents in Guangdong and Hong Kong) to the Mainland authorities to apply for the Regular Quotas. Upon the issuance of the Approval Notice to applicants by the Mainland authorities, they may apply to the Transport Department of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government for CRPs for the land control points endorsed on the Approval Notice. Vehicles with CRPs for the above designated control points are only permitted to travel between Guangdong and Hong Kong via the existing Lok Ma Chau Control Point or the soon-to-open new Huanggang Port between 0.00am and 6.30am daily.

     "Similar false information has surfaced from time to time in social media and messaging groups, repeatedly impersonating government announcements and falsely claiming that quotas are free from control point or eligibility restrictions to solicit clients. Such claims are particularly misleading to road users of both places amid the anticipated upcoming opening of the new Huanggang Port. The public should exercise heightened vigilance," the spokesman added.

     The HKSAR Government reiterated that arrangements regarding Guangdong-Hong Kong Regular Quotas and use of control points are serious issues which must be jointly deliberated by the governments of the two places holistically. There are currently no plans to adjust the arrangement of enabling cross-boundary vehicles with CRPs for designated control points to use the Lok Ma Chau Control Point/new Huanggang Port during the overnight period. Members of the public should refer to official announcements, especially regarding the opening arrangements for the new Huanggang Port, and verify messages carefully to guard against deception and avoid disruptions to travel plans.

item.title: Brussels ETO strengthens trade ties with Burgundy wine industry in France (with photos)
item.description:
The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Brussels (Brussels ETO), in collaboration with the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC), visited the Burgundy wine region in France from September 28 to 30 (Burgundy time) to promote Hong Kong's role as an international hub for wine trading.

     The visit covered key wine-producing areas in the Burgundy wine region. The Brussels ETO and the HKTDC held a number of meetings with the local government, wine producers as well as wine industry institutions to promote the vast opportunities in Hong Kong as the hub for wine trading, distribution and auction, and to exchange views on the latest developments in the global wine market as well as the local wine production industry.

     Speaking during a networking and promotional dinner with senior regional officials and industry representatives, the Special Representative for Hong Kong Economic and Trade Affairs to the European Union, Ms Shirley Yung, highlighted Hong Kong's standing as a world-leading hub for wine trading and auction, following the removal of wine duty in 2008 and the reduction of liquor duty in 2024.

     "Hong Kong's wine trading and auction activities are giving impetus to the development of other high value-added sectors such as logistics and storage, tourism as well as premium food and beverage consumption. We very much welcome the Burgundy wine trade to leverage Hong Kong's strategic position as the regional trading, distribution and auction hub to expand its market share in China and the wider Asia-Pacific region," Ms Yung added.

     During the visit, Ms Yung also extended her warm invitation to the Burgundy wine industry to visit Hong Kong, including for the Hong Kong Wine & Dine Festival in October every year, as well as the Hong Kong International Wine & Spirits Fair in November every year. Moreover, she promoted the Festival of Connoisseurs to the local wine industry, which will have its inaugural edition in November 2026 to showcase the art of premium lifestyles in Hong Kong.

     Burgundy is one of the world's most renowned wine regions, with a rich winemaking heritage rooted in its distinctive terroirs and traditions. About half of its wine is exported to international markets. The visit formed part of the Brussels ETO's ongoing efforts to foster exchanges between Hong Kong and Europe in the wine sector and identify opportunities for closer collaboration in wine business and wine tourism.

item.title: Import of poultry meat and products from areas in US and UK suspended
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (October 5) that in view of notifications from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) about outbreaks of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza in Big Stone County and Kandiyohi County of the State of Minnesota, Ravalli County of the State of Montana, and Barron County of the State of Wisconsin in the United States (US), and a notification from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs of the United Kingdom (UK) about an outbreak of highly pathogenic H5N5 avian influenza in the Isle of Lewis of Scotland in the UK, the CFS has instructed the trade to suspend the import of poultry meat and products (including poultry eggs) from the above-mentioned areas with immediate effect to protect public health in Hong Kong.
      
     A CFS spokesman said that according to the Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong imported about 24 190 tonnes of chilled and frozen poultry meat and about 20.2 million poultry eggs from the US, and about 340 tonnes of chilled and frozen poultry meat from the UK in the first six months of this year.
      
     "The CFS has contacted the American and British authorities over the issues and will closely monitor information issued by the WOAH and the relevant authorities on the avian influenza outbreaks. Appropriate action will be taken in response to the development of the situation," the spokesman said.

item.title: SCS visits Government Property Agency (with photos)
item.description:
The Secretary for the Civil Service, Mrs Ingrid Yeung, visited the Government Property Agency (GPA) this afternoon (October 5) to learn about the department's work in managing government properties and leveraging technology to enhance the quality and efficiency of services. She also met and exchanged views with staff representatives from various grades in the department.

     Accompanied by the Permanent Secretary for the Civil Service, Ms Shirley Lam, Mrs Yeung first met with the Government Property Administrator, Mr Raymond Sy, and other directorate staff, and received a briefing on the latest developments of the department's work on the use of government properties and enhancement of public spaces in joint-user government office buildings among other matters.

     Mrs Yeung then met with staff of the Property Management Division to learn about the latest situation of the management of government properties, including the preparatory work for the Hong Kong Port Area of the Huanggang Port Building conducted by the multidisciplinary team responsible for property management of the redeveloped Port. Mr Sy said that the department's staff have been working as one, in collaboration with the Security Bureau and other relevant departments, to ensure comprehensive preparation for the smooth opening of the Port.

     During the visit, the GPA staff introduced to Mrs Yeung the department's latest research and development in technology applications that aim to leverage AI to assist in the processing of large volumes of property management invoices and applications for repair and maintenance of property facilities, including the extraction and verification of data. This not only reduces the work of manual data input and checking to streamline workflow, but also enhances the accuracy of the vetting process. Staff can allocate their time more flexibly to follow up on complex cases and improve service quality.

     Mrs Yeung also watched a demonstration by staff of the Management Services Division of the in-house developed Mobile Site Inspection System (MSIS), a mobile application used in daily property inspections. The MSIS ensures standardisation of inspection items by listing the items to be inspected, while its report generation function not only streamlines writing and unifies report formatting, but also facilitates the systematic organisation of property inspection information. After processing by AI, the data will be uploaded to the government cloud, enabling staff to make use of big data analysis to study ways to further optimise services. Unlike in the past when paper documents such as property plans had to be carried during property inspections, staff now only need a tablet installed with the MSIS to view relevant property information, fill in inspection records, and take and upload inspection photos in a one-stop manner, with the application promptly generating an automated draft inspection report.

     Mrs Yeung said, "Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proposes to leverage AI technology to reform public administration. I encourage policy bureaux and departments to adopt an innovative spirit, integrate workflow, enhance overall efficiency, and build a more professional and efficient civil service." 

     Before concluding her visit, Mrs Yeung met with staff representatives from various grades in the department to exchange views on matters of concern to them.

item.title: HKSAR LegCo strongly opposes and disapproves of remarks by UK FCDO official on Hong Kong Alliance case
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Legislative Council Secretariat:

     A spokesperson for the Legislative Council (LegCo) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) today (October 5) expressed strong opposition to and disapproval of the untruthful remarks made by an official of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) of the United Kingdom (UK) responsible for Indo-Pacific affairs regarding the sentencing of the "Hong Kong Alliance" case. In a recent letter reply to members of the UK Parliament, the official smeared Hong Kong's judicial system and interfered in Hong Kong's affairs.
 
     The LegCo spokesperson stated that Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law. LegCo firmly supports the Court of First Instance of the High Court in handing down sentences in the case in accordance with the law, considering that the judgment demonstrates legal justice and strongly safeguards the HKSAR's constitutional order established by the Constitution of the People's Republic of China (PRC) (the Constitution) and the Basic Law of the HKSAR of the PRC (the Basic Law). LegCo resolutely opposes any foreign forces making malicious smears, slanderous attacks, and taking the opportunity to interfere in China's internal affairs regarding the case.
 
     The LegCo spokesperson reiterated that, as pointed out earlier by the HKSAR Government in response to the UK's so-called six-monthly report on Hong Kong, the core essence of the Sino-British Joint Declaration is about China's resumption of the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong. It did not authorise the UK to interfere in Hong Kong's affairs after its return to the motherland. Thereafter, the UK has no sovereignty, jurisdiction or right of supervision over Hong Kong.
 
     The LegCo spokesperson pointed out that the allegation, which was made by the UK FCDO's official responsible for Indo-Pacific affairs, that the defendants in the case were convicted merely for "peaceful acts of remembrance" completely disregards facts and misleads the public. The court pointed out in its reasons for sentence that the defendants were not on trial for their political thoughts or acts prior to the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL). The convictions were purely because, after the HKNSL came into effect, they continued to pursue the goal of overthrowing and undermining the leadership of the Communist Party of China (CPC) as established under the Constitution by committing various incitement criminal acts. Those acts attempted to cause Hong Kong citizens to lose trust in the Communist Party, thereby achieving the objective of undermining the fundamental system of the state, gravely endangering national security. The UK official's attempt to glorify criminal acts endangering national security as peaceful activities is a blatant trampling on the spirit of the rule of law.
 
     The LegCo spokesperson also reiterated that the Constitution is the fundamental law of the state, clearly specifying that the CPC's leadership is the core and foundation of the state's constitutional order. No country's constitution allows its citizens to subvert the established constitutional order and fundamental system of the state. The UK itself maintains various stringent laws safeguarding national security, yet makes unreasonable criticisms against the legitimate measures of the HKSAR in safeguarding national security in accordance with the law. This is a typical act of hypocrisy with double standards. The LegCo spokesperson requests the British side immediately stops the acts of interfering in Hong Kong's affairs.
 
     In fact, since the implementation of the HKNSL and the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, the cornerstone of Hong Kong's rule of law has become more solid, and the various freedoms lawfully enjoyed by citizens have received more substantial protection. Various international indicators and rankings show that Hong Kong is a safe and stable city suitable for living and investment. As an integral member of the HKSAR's governing team, LegCo firmly supports the HKSAR Government in fully and faithfully implementing laws safeguarding national security, safeguarding high-quality development of the country and Hong Kong with high-level security, and ensuring the steadfast and successful implementation of the "one country, two systems" principle.

item.title: HKMA hosts CargoX Solution Day to promote regional trade data connectivity (with photos)
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority:
 
     The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) today (October 5) successfully organised the CargoX Solution Day. The event served as a platform for key stakeholders in the cargo and trade data ecosystem to exchange insights and showcase the innovative solutions in enhancing trade data connectivity to regional levels under the CargoX Pilot Programme.
      
     Themed "From local to regional trade data connectivity: shaping the future of trade finance through innovative CargoX pilots", the Solution Day attracted over 300 industry professionals from banks, cargo and trade data providers, government agencies and partners of Commercial Data Interchange (CDI). The event featured keynote speeches, panel discussions and solution presentations, focusing on strengthening trade data connectivity with Hong Kong's key trading partners, such as the Chinese Mainland and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) economies, as well as integrating CDI with key government cargo and trade data platforms.
      
     A highlight of the CargoX Solution Day was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the HKMA and the PAA Digital Trade Alliance (PAA) (Note 1) to promote trade finance digitalisation. The two parties will commence joint innovation projects on enhancing cargo and trade data connectivity between Hong Kong and PAA member economies, thereby catalysing data-driven innovation in financial services and enhancing trade finance availability in the region.
      
     During the Solution Day, the HKMA also shared results achieved under the CargoX Pilot Programme, particularly its progress in enhancing connectivity with key trade corridors. In collaboration with the Shanghai Data Bureau (SDB), the HKMA has successfully established a link-up between CDI and a digital trade platform developed by the SDB. Known as "CargoX Connect", this collaboration has enabled five pilot banks (Note 2) to access and utilise trade declaration data from the Yangtze River Delta region, serving as the first pilot cohort. This development facilitates various trade finance processes, such as trade verification and due diligence on trade counterparts, resulting in faster loan drawdowns for Hong Kong businesses engaging in both onshore and offshore trade. To date, this pilot has enabled the approval of ten trade finance loans amounting to HK$180 million. The HKMA intends to extend this successful model to other provinces and cities in the Chinese Mainland as the next phase of development.
      
     Building on these encouraging developments in collaboration with the SDB and the PAA, through CargoX, the HKMA will continue to leverage Hong Kong's role as a super-connector to strengthen trade data connectivity along key corridors, including the Chinese Mainland and ASEAN. The ultimate goal is to enhance the transparency of cross-border trade transactions, thereby unlocking trade finance opportunities and supporting the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the region.
      
     Deputy Chief Executive of the HKMA Mr Howard Lee said, "Today's CargoX Solution Day serves as a vital platform to showcase how the CargoX Pilot Programme is translating strategic recommendations into tangible actions. Building on the encouraging progress of the CargoX pilot projects, the signing of the MoU with the PAA marks a significant milestone in our endeavour to enhance regional trade data connectivity, including ASEAN economies, for more streamlined SME trade financing. By leveraging our CDI data infrastructure, CargoX will continue to expand from local to regional levels, building a more efficient and inclusive digital trade ecosystem across borders. This ultimately contributes to SME growth and fosters seamless international trade."
      
     The Chair of the PAA, Tan Sri Syed Zainal Abidin Syed Mohamed Tahir, said, "The signing of this MoU with the HKMA marks a transformative step forward for cross-border trade finance in the region. By seamlessly bridging the PAA's robust regional network with Hong Kong's cutting-edge CDI infrastructure, we are unlocking the true power of data-driven finance. Together, we will eliminate the traditional frictions in international trade, giving SMEs across ASEAN and neighbouring economies unprecedented access to capital. We are excited to co-create a more inclusive, resilient, and fully digitised regional trade ecosystem."

Note 1: The PAA is a global alliance comprising trade single window operators and e-commerce service providers from 15 economies, including ASEAN member states.

Note 2: These pilot banks include Bank of China (Hong Kong), Hang Seng Bank, The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (Asia) and Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong).

item.title: Advisory Council on the Environment fully supports Hong Kong's First Five Year Plan to continue to drive green transition in Hong Kong
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Advisory Council on the Environment:

     The Advisory Council on the Environment (ACE) discussed at its meeting today (October 5) the major strategies and initiatives on environmental protection and related issues set out in the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) (Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan) and the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address (Policy Address). The ACE unanimously supports the strategies and initiatives.

     The ACE is pleased to note that four of the five binding indicators set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan are environment-related, covering carbon intensity, the share of zero-carbon energy, the average concentration of fine suspended particulates (PM2.5), and Hong Kong’s surface water quality, demonstrating the Government’s determination to build Hong Kong into a green and liveable city and drive its future green transition. At the meeting, members had in-depth discussions on various environmental protection and ecological issues and offered recommendations to the Government.  

     The Chairman of the ACE, Professor John Chai, said, "The ACE believes that the Government will implement various measures in accordance with Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address to push forward Hong Kong’s green transition and foster green innovation continuously, thereby aligning with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. These efforts will contribute to building a Beautiful China and a Beautiful Hong Kong, as well as realising the green transition and high-quality economic development of the nation."

     Professor Chai added that the ACE will continue, as always, to provide professional advice to the Government on various environmental issues and drive the implementation of sustainable development and green transition in Hong Kong. The ACE will fully support and align with Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan, actively contributing to the future development of both the nation and Hong Kong.

item.title: DH announces latest situation regarding Legionnaires' disease cases
item.description:
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (October 5) reported the latest number of Legionnaires' disease (LD) cases, and reminded the public of the importance of using and maintaining properly designed man-made water systems, adding that susceptible groups should strictly observe relevant precautions.

     From September 27 to October 3, the CHP recorded two LD cases, involving one male and one female. Details are as follows:
 
  • a 67-year-old male living in Southern District with underlying illnesses, classified as a community-acquired case; and
  • a 55-year-old female with underlying illnesses who travelled to the Chinese Mainland during the incubation period, classified as an imported case.

     ​The CHP is conducting epidemiological investigations to identify the potential sources of infection and high-risk exposure. An initial investigation revealed that the aforesaid cases are sporadic cases. No epidemiological linkages have been established between these cases and other confirmed cases previously recorded in Hong Kong.

     As of October 3, 153 LD cases had been recorded this year. In 2025 and 2024, there were 167 and 135 LD cases respectively.

     Men, people aged over 50, smokers, alcoholics and persons with weakened immunity are more susceptible to LD. Some situations may also increase the risk of infection, including poor maintenance of water systems; living in areas with old water systems, cooling towers or fountains; using electric water heaters, whirlpool spas or hot water spring spas; and recent stays in hotels or ships.

     Legionellae are found in various environmental settings and grow well in warm water (20 to 45 degrees Celsius). They can be found in aqueous environments such as water tanks, hot and cold water systems, cooling towers, whirlpool spas, water fountains, humidifiers and home respiratory devices that support breathing. People may become infected when they breathe in contaminated droplets (aerosols) and mist generated by artificial water systems, or when handling garden soil, compost and potting mixes.
 
     Immunocompromised persons should:
 
  • Use sterile or boiled water for drinking, tooth brushing and mouth rinsing;
  • Avoid using humidifiers, or other mist- or aerosol-generating devices; and
  • If using humidifiers, or other mist- or aerosol-generating devices, fill the water tank with only sterile or cooled freshly boiled water, and not water directly from the tap. Also, clean and maintain humidifiers/devices regularly according to manufacturers' instructions. Never leave stagnant water in a humidifier/device. Empty the water tank, wipe all surfaces dry, and change the water daily.

     ​The public should observe the health advice below:
 
  • Observe personal hygiene;
  • Do not smoke and avoid alcohol consumption;
  • Strainers in water taps and shower heads should be inspected, cleaned, descaled and disinfected regularly or at a frequency recommended by the manufacturer;
  • If a fresh-water plumbing system is properly maintained, it is not necessary to install domestic water filters. Use of water filters is not encouraged as clogging occurs easily, which can promote growth of micro-organisms. In case water filters are used, the pore size should be 0.2 micrometres (µm) or less and the filter needs to be changed periodically according to the manufacturer's recommendations;
  • Drain and clean water tanks of buildings at least quarterly;
  • Drain or purge for at least one minute infrequently used water outlets (e.g. water taps, shower heads and hot water outlets) and stagnant points of the pipework weekly or before use;
  • Seek and follow doctors' professional advice regarding the use and maintenance of home respiratory devices and use only sterile water (not distilled or tap water) to clean and fill the reservoir. Clean and maintain the device regularly according to the manufacturer's instructions. After cleaning/disinfection, rinse the device with sterile water, cooled freshly boiled water or water filtered with 0.2 µm filters. Never leave stagnant water in the device. Empty the water tank, keep all surfaces dry, and change the water daily; and
  • When handling garden soil, compost and potting mixes:
  1. Wear gloves and a face mask;
  2. Water gardens and compost gently using low pressure;
  3. Open composted potting mixes slowly and make sure the opening is directed away from the face;
  4. Wet the soil to reduce dust when potting plants; and
  5. Avoid working in poorly ventilated places such as enclosed greenhouses.
 
     The public may visit the CHP's LD page, the Code of Practice for Prevention of LD and the Housekeeping Guidelines for Cold and Hot Water Systems for Building Management of the Prevention of LD Committee, and the CHP's risk-based strategy for prevention and control of LD.

     Additionally, as smokers and alcoholics are more susceptible to LD, the Government urges members of the public to quit smoking and avoid drinking. Members of the public may call the DH Integrated Smoking Cessation Hotline at 1833 183, which is answered by registered nurses who provide professional counselling and referrals to a wide range of free smoking cessation services. The public may also visit the smoking cessation thematic website (www.livetobaccofree.hk) for more information on smoking cessation. The DH has also developed and promulgated the Alcohol Screening and Brief Intervention tool to primary healthcare service providers to facilitate the early identification and management of at-risk drinkers. For information on alcohol-related harm, please visit the DH's Change for Health website.

item.title: InnoCarnival 2026 to run from October 24 to November 1 (with photos)
item.description:
Organised by the Innovation and Technology Commission (ITC), the InnoCarnival 2026 (IC 2026) will be held for nine consecutive days from October 24 to November 1 at the Hong Kong Science Park with the theme of "Lead with I&T Dream to Fly High". Public admission is free. The event is receiving support from over 40 programme partners, including local universities, research and development (R&D) centres, government departments and other organisations. By showcasing a number of local innovations and research achievements, the event will offer the public an opportunity to experience the vibrant innovation and technology (I&T) development scene in Hong Kong, as well as the diverse applications of these innovations.

     Speaking at the media preview for IC 2026 today (October 5), the Commissioner for Innovation and Technology, Mr Ivan Lee, said, "Dr Lai Ka-ying, Hong Kong's first payload specialist, participated in our country's space mission in May this year, proving that the dream of space exploration is not out of reach. This year's Carnival will feature an aerospace thematic zone to showcase research projects of local universities and their contributions to our country's space exploration missions, hoping to inspire more young people to explore the unknown and pursue their dreams."

     The media preview exhibited the R&D projects of several participating teams. Project team representatives presented their inspirational ideas, R&D processes, features and functions, and project applications. These projects include the greenhouse gas monitoring instrument "MUSICO", spearheaded by the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and operated by Dr Lai on the Tiangong Space Station. This fully demonstrates the research capability of local universities' R&D teams in the fields of aerospace technology, as well as their important contributions to the country's space mission.

     In addition, the Hong Kong Productivity Council introduced its "Autonomous Air-ground Cooperative Tunnel Inspector". With the synergy of AI, robotics and total-station positioning techniques, the system is employed in the Trunk Road T2 and Cha Kwo Ling Tunnel project to carry out tunnel inspections, bringing intelligence, automation and digital advancement to tunnel inspections in Hong Kong. This system won the Gold Award at the 2025 Edison Awards, gaining international recognition.

     Representatives from Po Leung Kuk Celine Ho Yam Tong College introduced the "Hydroguard - AI-powered Water-quality Monitoring Platform", a compact AI-powered water quality monitoring platform that integrates automated screening, data collection and real-time environmental monitoring. The platform not only improves the accuracy, efficiency and accessibility of water quality testing, but also enables a faster identification of and response to contamination risks, supporting safer and more sustainable water resource management. 

     IC 2026 exhibition booths will be set up to showcase local I&T achievements, some of them with interactive games. A diverse line-up of about 150 workshops and over 10 webinars across various subjects including aerospace technology and AI will be available during the Carnival. All activities are free of charge. Some of the activities require preregistration, which will begin at 10.30am on October 6 (Tuesday). Details are available at the thematic webpage (innocarnival.hk). Places are limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Members of the public are most welcome to join. During the Carnival, free shuttle bus services will be provided between Hong Kong Science Park and various districts, including MTR University Station, Tai Wai Station, Kowloon Tong Station, and Admiralty Station, as well as the new routes at Yuen Long Station and Tseung Kwan O Station, offering convenient access for visitors.

item.title: Inspection of aquatic products imported from Japan
item.description:
In response to the Japanese Government's plan to discharge nuclear-contaminated water at the Fukushima Nuclear Power Station, the Director of Food and Environmental Hygiene issued a Food Safety Order which prohibits all aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds originating from the 10 metropolis/prefectures, namely Tokyo, Fukushima, Ibaraki, Miyagi, Chiba, Gunma, Tochigi, Niigata, Nagano and Saitama, from being imported into and supplied in Hong Kong.
 
     For other Japanese aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds that are not prohibited from being imported into Hong Kong, the Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department is conducting comprehensive radiological tests to verify that the radiation levels of these products do not exceed the guideline levels before they are allowed to be supplied in the market.
 
     From noon on October 2 to noon today (October 5), the CFS conducted tests on the radiological levels of 427 food samples imported from Japan, which were of the "aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt" category. No sample was found to have exceeded the safety limit. Details can be found on the CFS's thematic website titled "Control Measures on Foods Imported from Japan" (www.cfs.gov.hk/english/programme/programme_rafs/programme_rafs_fc_01_30_Nuclear_Event_and_Food_Safety.html).
 
     In parallel, the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) has also tested 150 samples of local catch for radiological levels. All the samples passed the tests. Details can be found on the AFCD's website (www.afcd.gov.hk/english/fisheries/Radiological_testing/Radiological_Test.html).
 
     The Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) has also enhanced the environmental monitoring of the local waters. No anomaly has been detected so far. For details, please refer to the HKO's website (www.hko.gov.hk/en/radiation/monitoring/seawater.html).
 
     From August 24, 2023, to noon today, the CFS and the AFCD have conducted tests on the radiological levels of 265 118 samples of food imported from Japan (including 165 179 samples of aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt) and 56 558 samples of local catch respectively. All the samples passed the tests.

item.title: Company and its director fined $66,000 for contravening Employment Ordinance
item.description:
AD Fortune Communications Limited and its director were prosecuted by the Labour Department (LD) for violating the requirements under the Employment Ordinance (EO). The company and its director pleaded guilty at the Eastern Magistrates' Courts today (October 5) and were fined a total sum of $66,000. The company and its director were also ordered to pay the employees concerned an outstanding sum of about $287,000.

     The company wilfully and without reasonable excuse contravened the requirements of the EO, failing to pay four employees' wages within seven days after the expiry of the wage periods and termination of the employment contracts, totalling about $190,000, as well as the awarded sums totalling about $287,000 within 14 days after the date set by the Labour Tribunal (LT). The director was also prosecuted and convicted for her consent, connivance or neglect in the above offences.

     "The ruling will disseminate a strong message to all employers, directors and responsible officers of companies that they have to pay wages, termination payments and sums awarded by the LT or the Minor Employment Claims Adjudication Board to employees within the statutory time limit stipulated in the EO," a spokesman for the LD said.

     "The LD will not tolerate these offences and will spare no effort in enforcing the law and safeguarding employees' statutory rights," the spokesman added.

item.title: A hot and relatively dry September
item.description:
Attributed to the stronger-than-normal upper-air anticyclone over southern China, September 2026 was hotter and drier than usual. The monthly mean minimum temperature of 27.1 degrees was 1.0 degree above the normal and the fifth highest on record for September. The monthly mean temperature of 28.8 degrees and mean maximum temperature of 31.8 degrees were 0.9 degree and 1.3 degrees above their respective normals and both were one of the 10th highest on record for September.  Moreover, the monthly mean relative humidity of 74 per cent was four percentage points below the normal of 78 per cent and was one of the sixth lowest on record for September. Rainfall in the month was only 94.3 millimetres, about 29 per cent of the normal of 321.4 millimetres. The accumulated rainfall in the first nine months of the year was 2 451.9 millimetres, about nine per cent above the normal of 2 242.8 millimetres for the same period.

     After Saudel re-intensified into a tropical depression on the last day of August, it moved northeastwards across the northern part of the South China Sea on September 1 and skirted about 200 kilometres southeast of Hong Kong. It further intensified into a tropical storm on the next day before making landfall over Zhangzhou, Fujian, on the morning of September 3. It then moved across the eastern part of inland Guangdong and weakened gradually. Locally, under the combined effect of Saudel and the northeast monsoon, there were occasional strong winds offshore and on high ground on September 1. There were occasional squally showers and thunderstorms. Around 20 millimetres of rainfall were generally recorded over the territory, and rainfall even exceeded 40 millimetres over the eastern part of the New Territories. With the departure of Saudel, showers decreased and there were sunny intervals during the day on September 2 and 3.

     Winds over Hong Kong were weak during the next five days. Apart from isolated showers, local weather became generally fine on September 4 and 5. However, a band of clouds covered Guangdong on September 6 and brought a few showers to the territory. There were more showers in some areas in the morning. Around 10 millimetres of rainfall were recorded over many places, and rainfall even exceeded 40 millimetres over the northeastern part of the New Territories. Under light wind conditions, daytime heating triggered showers over inland Guangdong the next day. The heat-triggered showers moved southwards and affected the territory that afternoon with more than 20 millimetres of rainfall recorded over Yuen Long and Tsuen Wan Districts. With the thinning out of the cloud bands, the weather of Hong Kong turned mainly fine apart from isolated showers on September 8.

     The northeast monsoon affected southern China in the next four days. Locally, the weather was dry during the day with a mixture of sunny periods and a few showers. Showers were heavier with more than 20 millimetres over North District on the morning of September 10. Under the showers in the small hours on September 11, the temperature at the Observatory dropped to a minimum of 25.5 degrees, the lowest of the month. With plenty of sunshine, it was very hot on September 12. Under the combined effect of a strong northeast monsoon and a tropical depression over the seas to the east of Vietnam, local winds strengthened gradually on September 12 and persisted until the next day. Local weather was mainly cloudy with sunny intervals and a few showers on September 13.

     The northeast monsoon moderated on September 14 and a band of clouds over the coast of Guangdong brought a few showers to the territory. Showers were heavier in some areas with thunderstorms. More than 40 millimetres of rainfall were recorded over parts of the North District, Tuen Mun and Kowloon. Under the influence of a replenishment of the northeast monsoon, local weather was mainly cloudy with a few showers on September 15 and became generally fine on the following two days. It was dry in the afternoon of September 17. Affected by an anticyclone aloft, local weather remained dry during the day and generally fine from September 18 to 20. It was very hot on September 19 and 20.

     Winds were weak over the coast of Guangdong on September 21. Locally, it was still very hot with sunny periods. Upper-air disturbances brought a few showers and thunderstorms to the territory on September 22. Around 5 millimetres of rainfall were recorded over Hong Kong Island and parts of the New Territories East. Under the influence of the northeast monsoon, the weather of Hong Kong was generally fine apart from isolated showers in the mornings on September 23 and 24. The northeast monsoon moderated and an anticyclone aloft continued to bring mainly fine weather to the coast of Guangdong from September 25 to 30. Local weather remained dry during the day and generally fine during the last six days of the month, apart from isolated showers from September 28 to 30. It was also very hot on September 29 and 30. With abundant sunshine, the temperature at the Observatory rose to a maximum of 34.2 degrees on the afternoon of September 30, the highest of the month.

item.title: RTHK launches new media platform and mascot Wavee

     The Director of Broadcasting, Ms Angelina Kwan, said that RTHK is capitalising on the advantages of new media's broad coverage and fast production and dissemination capabilities to provide the public with diverse online content, strengthening its communications reach while fully demonstrating the extensive application of AI technology. Through the new media platform and Wavee, RTHK hopes to inject greater dynamism and approachability into its offerings, drawing a wider audience, especially the younger generation, to tune in to RTHK's productions.
 
     The new media platform presents Hong Kong's strengths and community character from multiple perspectives, with specially curated content organised around five key themes. "Wa~ So Hong Kong" ventures deep into local communities to uncover heartwarming human stories; "Wa~ So Cheeky" takes a light-hearted look at the lovable and endearing side of Hong Kong; and "Wa~ So Chill" introduces residents and visitors alike to the city's signature events, cultural attractions and local culinary scene. Through these specially produced titles, RTHK aims to promote Hong Kong and champion its spirit in an engaging and accessible manner. In addition, "Wa~ So Classic" leverages AI technology to restore precious archival footage from RTHK's archives, presenting Hong Kong's remarkable development journey through a compelling then-and-now format. Beyond serving as the emblem of the new media platform, Wavee will take on an important ambassadorial role for RTHK, appearing across its new media content, television and radio programmes, and public events.

item.title: Investigation report on accident involving Niviuk Artik R paraglider published
item.description:
The Air Accident Investigation Authority (AAIA) today (October 5) published the Investigation Report IVR-2026-04 on the investigation into an impact with a grass area accident involving a Niviuk Artik R paraglider preparing for landing at Ngong Ping, Ma On Shan, on February 11, 2025.

     At 12.10pm that day, the paraglider pilot took off solo from a paragliding area in Ngong Ping. After flying for about 23 minutes and preparing for landing, the paraglider impacted the grass area. The pilot sustained injuries and fell into a coma.

     The investigation found that he exerted too much left brake on the EN-C glider he flew to adjust his landing approach, probably due to negative transfer from his extensive and recent experience flying EN-B paragliders. As a result, the left side of the wing stalled, causing the paraglider to enter a left-hand spin and eventually impact the grass area.

     The investigation team has issued one safety recommendation to the Hong Kong China Paragliding Association and the International Paragliding Association. The recommendation is to alert all participants of paragliding in Hong Kong, when transitioning between different classes of gliders, on the importance of taking defensive measures to mitigate the risks of negative transfer.

     The investigation was conducted by a team of professional investigators in strict adherence to international standards established by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). "The objective of the investigation was to identify the circumstances and causes of the accident with a view to preventing a recurrence," an AAIA spokesperson said.

     Throughout the investigation, all parties concerned were properly consulted on the report. The report is available for downloading on the AAIA webpage (www.tlb.gov.hk/aaia/eng/investigation_reports/index.html).

item.title: Investigation report on accident involving BogdanFly X-wing paraglider published
item.description:
The Air Accident Investigation Authority (AAIA) today (October 5) published the Investigation Report IVR-2026-03 on the investigation into a collision with terrain accident involving a BogdanFly X-wing paraglider during flight at Sunset Peak, Lantau, on June 17, 2024.

     At 2.30pm that day, the paraglider pilot took off solo from a paragliding area in Sunset Peak. He later collided with terrain and was stuck in a tree on a slope at Sunset Peak. He did not survive.

     The investigation found that he probably lost effective pilot control of the paraglider under strong lift and in cloud, which resulted in a collision with terrain that rendered multiple injuries to him.

     The investigation team has issued one safety recommendation to the Hong Kong China Paragliding Association and the International Paragliding Association. The recommendation is to re-emphasise to all Hong Kong paragliding participants on the utmost importance of taking a thorough approach when conducting a comprehensive risk assessment to ensure that the risks are as low as reasonably practical.

     The investigation was conducted by a team of professional investigators in strict adherence to international standards established by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). "The objective of the investigation was to identify the circumstances and causes of the accident with a view to preventing a recurrence," an AAIA spokesperson said.

     Throughout the investigation, all parties concerned were properly consulted on the report. The report is available for downloading on the AAIA webpage (www.tlb.gov.hk/aaia/eng/investigation_reports/index.html). 

     The AAIA, an independent investigation authority formed under the Transport and Logistics Bureau, is responsible for the investigation of civil aircraft accidents and incidents in accordance with the Hong Kong Civil Aviation (Investigation of Accidents) Regulations (Cap. 448B) and with reference to the ICAO standards.

item.title: Inaugural list of "New Industrialisation Elite Enterprises" announced
item.description:
The Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau today (October 5) announced the inaugural list of selected enterprises under the New Industrialisation Elite Enterprises Nurturing Scheme (the Scheme).  A total of eight enterprises have been selected as the inaugural "New Industrialisation Elite Enterprises".

　　Echoing the direction set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the 2026 Policy Address to accelerate the development of a new industrialisation system, the Scheme aims to nurture leading enterprises in emerging and future industries for Hong Kong. It is also an important initiative in advancing the integrated development of education, technology, talent and industry. Selected enterprises are awarded the honorary title of "New Industrialisation Elite Enterprise", which enables them to more effectively access market resources and forces through the Scheme platform, and hence enhance their market visibility and recognition.

　　The Scheme received over 100 nominations. The nominated enterprises span a wide range of business sectors, including life and health technology; AI and robotics; semiconductors and smart devices; digitalisation, upgrading and transformation; as well as future and sustainable development. They also include enterprises from industries with traditional strengths that leverage innovation and technology for upgrading and transformation, fully demonstrating the diverse vitality and thriving ecosystem of Hong Kong's new industrialisation development.

　　The assessment was based on three core selection criteria, namely the enterprises' research and development capabilities, growth potential, and local contribution and ecosystem impact. Following thorough discussion and careful assessment by the assessment committee, eight enterprises have been selected as the inaugural "New Industrialisation Elite Enterprises". The list of selected enterprises is set out in the Annex.

　　The Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, Professor Sun Dong, said, "The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government attaches great importance to the nurturing and development of local innovation and technology enterprises. The New Industrialisation Elite Enterprises Nurturing Scheme aims to focus on supporting and nurturing a group of high-growth enterprises developing in Hong Kong. Through the Scheme, the Government hopes to enhance the market recognition and visibility for the 'Made in Hong Kong' enterprise brand, thereby supporting the future development of enterprises."

item.description:

Land registration
